const RJX_CUES=[["People", "Describe a person who has helped you learn something", ["who the person is", "what they helped you learn", "how they helped you", "why you remember this person"]], ["Places", "Describe a place you enjoy visiting", ["where it is", "how often you go", "what you do there", "why you enjoy it"]], ["Experiences", "Describe a time you solved a difficult problem", ["what the problem was", "where you were", "what you did", "how you felt afterwards"]], ["Objects", "Describe something useful you own", ["what it is", "when you got it", "how you use it", "why it is useful"]], ["Technology", "Describe a piece of technology you use often", ["what it is", "when you use it", "what it helps you do", "why it matters to you"]], ["Learning", "Describe a skill you would like to improve", ["what the skill is", "why you want it", "how you could improve", "how it would help you"]], ["Work", "Describe a job you think is interesting", ["what the job is", "what people do", "what skills it needs", "why it interests you"]], ["Travel", "Describe a journey you remember well", ["where you went", "who you travelled with", "what happened", "why you remember it"]], ["Food", "Describe a meal you really enjoyed", ["what you ate", "where you ate it", "who was with you", "why it was memorable"]], ["Events", "Describe an event you were happy to attend", ["what it was", "where it happened", "who was there", "why you enjoyed it"]], ["Media", "Describe a film, programme or video you recommend", ["what it is", "what it is about", "when you watched it", "why you recommend it"]], ["Future", "Describe something you hope to achieve", ["what it is", "why it matters", "what you need to do", "how you will feel if you achieve it"]]];
const RJX_IELTS=[["Speaking Part 1", "Short personal questions, natural answers and vocabulary extension."], ["Speaking Part 2", "Cue cards, one-minute preparation and two-minute speaking practice."], ["Speaking Part 3", "Developed opinions, comparisons, causes, effects and examples."], ["Writing Task 1", "Overview writing, comparisons, trends and clear data language."], ["Writing Task 2", "Essay planning, thesis statements, topic sentences and development."], ["Reading", "Skimming, scanning, matching headings, inference and time control."], ["Listening", "Prediction, distractors, spelling, note completion and section strategy."], ["Band 7–9 Language", "Precision, coherence, flexible grammar and natural vocabulary."]];
const RJX_TOEIC=[["Picture Description", "Choose accurate sentences for workplace and everyday scenes."], ["Question–Response", "Recognise natural short answers and common distractors."], ["Conversations", "Track purpose, detail, location and next actions."], ["Talks & Announcements", "Follow workplace messages, schedules and instructions."], ["Incomplete Sentences", "Grammar and vocabulary in business contexts."], ["Text Completion", "Cohesion, vocabulary and grammar across short texts."], ["Reading Comprehension", "Emails, notices, adverts, schedules and multi-text sets."], ["Business Vocabulary", "Meetings, invoices, travel, recruitment, logistics and customer service."]];

const RJX_EXAM_BANK={
  "Speaking Part 1":{
    teach:"IELTS Speaking Part 1 is a short interview about familiar topics. Strong answers are direct, natural and extended just enough to show your English without sounding memorised.",
    strategy:["Answer the question immediately","Add one useful detail","Give a short reason or example","Use natural linking rather than a memorised speech"],
    model:"Question: Do you enjoy cooking? Model: Yes, I do, especially at weekends. I usually make simple Thai or Italian food because I enjoy trying different flavours.",
    questions:[
      ["Which Part 1 answer is best?",["Yes.","Yes, I do. I usually cook at weekends because I have more time.","I would like to discuss the advantages and disadvantages of cooking."],1,"A good Part 1 answer is direct, natural and briefly developed."],
      ["What should you avoid in Part 1?",["Answering the question directly","Adding a relevant reason","Giving a long memorised speech"],2,"Part 1 should sound conversational, not rehearsed."],
      ["Which phrase sounds natural for extending an answer?",["One reason is that...","According to the aforementioned issue...","This essay will discuss..."],0,"'One reason is that...' is a natural spoken extension."]
    ]
  },
  "Speaking Part 2":{
    teach:"Part 2 gives you one minute to prepare and up to two minutes to speak. The goal is to organise ideas quickly and keep speaking in a clear sequence.",
    strategy:["Use the bullet points as a safety net","Write keywords, not full sentences","Tell the answer like a short story","Use time markers and descriptive details"],
    model:"A simple structure is: introduce the topic → describe where/when → explain what happened → say why it mattered to you.",
    questions:[
      ["During the one-minute preparation, what is best to write?",["A complete essay","Keywords and a simple structure","Nothing at all"],1,"Keywords are faster to scan while you are speaking."],
      ["What is the main speaking goal in Part 2?",["Speak continuously and organise ideas","Give one short sentence","Use as many idioms as possible"],0,"Fluency and organised development matter more than forcing difficult language."],
      ["Which sequence is most useful?",["Introduction → details → reason/feeling","Conclusion → random detail → introduction","Vocabulary list → silence → answer"],0,"A clear sequence helps you keep talking naturally."]
    ]
  },
  "Speaking Part 3":{
    teach:"Part 3 asks broader, more analytical questions. Strong answers usually include an opinion, explanation, example and sometimes a comparison or consequence.",
    strategy:["State a clear position","Explain why","Use a real or hypothetical example","Compare when appropriate","Consider causes, effects or future change"],
    model:"I think public transport will become more important because cities are becoming more crowded. For example, reliable trains can reduce the number of cars entering city centres.",
    questions:[
      ["Which answer shape suits Part 3 best?",["Opinion → reason → example","Yes/No only","A memorised personal story with no link to the question"],0,"Part 3 rewards developed, relevant ideas."],
      ["Part 3 questions are usually...",["More analytical than Part 1","Only about spelling","Exactly the same as Part 2 cue cards"],0,"Part 3 moves towards discussion and analysis."],
      ["Which linker is useful for contrast?",["However","Yesterday","Blue"],0,"'However' can signal a contrasting point."]
    ]
  },
  "Writing Task 1":{
    teach:"Academic Task 1 requires you to summarise visual information. A strong response selects the main features, gives a clear overview and compares important data instead of describing every number.",
    strategy:["Paraphrase the task","Write a clear overview","Group similar features","Use comparisons and accurate trend language","Do not add personal opinions"],
    model:"Overall, sales increased in all three regions, although the rise was most significant in the north.",
    questions:[
      ["What is essential in Academic Task 1?",["A clear overview","Your personal opinion","A conclusion recommending action"],0,"The overview identifies the main trends or features."],
      ["Which sentence is a useful comparison?",["Sales in A were higher than in B.","I think A is better.","The chart is very nice."],0,"Task 1 needs objective comparison language."],
      ["What should you avoid?",["Selecting key data","Grouping information","Listing every number with no overview"],2,"A data-by-data list usually lacks meaningful summarising."]
    ]
  },
  "Writing Task 2":{
    teach:"Task 2 is an essay. Strong writing answers the exact question, gives a clear position, uses focused paragraphs and develops each main idea with explanation and evidence.",
    strategy:["Analyse every part of the question","Choose a clear position","Plan two or three main ideas","Use one central idea per body paragraph","Explain and exemplify each point"],
    model:"Topic sentence: One major benefit of remote work is the time employees save by avoiding a daily commute.",
    questions:[
      ["What should a body paragraph normally contain?",["One clear main idea developed with explanation","Five unrelated ideas","Only a quotation"],0,"Focused development improves coherence."],
      ["What should your thesis do?",["State your overall position or response","List every vocabulary word you know","Repeat the question word for word"],0,"The thesis tells the reader your main response."],
      ["Which is most important?",["Answering the exact task","Using the longest words possible","Writing a memorised essay"],0,"Task response depends on directly answering the question."]
